QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_41

question.text: Maximum Drawdown (MDD) of an AIF is calculated as:

answer.text: Standard deviation of negative returns only
The difference between Gross IRR and Net IRR

explanation.text: The Logic: Maximum Drawdown equals (Trough Value − Peak Value) / Peak Value and measures the peak-to-trough decline of the fund, expressed as a percentage of the peak. The Trap: Option A is downside deviation (used in the Sortino ratio). Option C is a fee-drag concept. Option D measures a single-day loss, not a peak-to-trough decline. Note: The workbook also notes that MDD does not show how long the fund takes to recover from a drawdown.
